textSlots.defaultValue: Founded in 2015 by Dr. Chris Monroe and Dr. Jungsang Kim, IonQ emerged from more than 30 years of academic research and foundational breakthroughs licensed from the University of Maryland and Duke University. textSlots.label: TECHNOLOGY / section2 / intro / intro
textSlots.defaultValue: Most quantum computers rely on superconducting circuits or exotic materials. IonQ takes a simpler, more powerful approach: we use single atoms—identical, stable, and natural—as the building blocks of computation.

textSlots.label: TECHNOLOGY / nav / navRight / navMenu
textSlots.defaultValue: Products   Company   Resources   Careers   Roadmap   Blog

textSlots.label: TECHNOLOGY / section2b / meetTitle / meetTitle
textSlots.defaultValue:
Meet our newest and most
powerful quantum computers

textSlots.label: TECHNOLOGY / hero / pre / pre
textSlots.defaultValue: Quantum built on nature’s most perfect building block:

textSlots.label: TECHNOLOGY / section2b / meetBody / meetBody
textSlots.defaultValue: Our latest systems are built for performance and practicality, enabling partners to solve their largest and most complex real-world business problems.

textSlots.label: TECHNOLOGY / section1 / col1 / col1t
textSlots.defaultValue:
At its core, a quantum computer is a machine that uses a quantum system, like the spin of an electron, to do a very specific type of math.

This math takes advantage of the uniquely complex behavior of quantum systems, namely entanglement and superposition, to perform calculations that are fundamentally unlike the calculations ordinary computers based on classical physics can perform.

textSlots.label: TECHNOLOGY / section1 / col2 / col2t
textSlots.defaultValue:
Many quantum hardware developers use "synthetic" quantum systems for their quantum bits (qubits for short), like loops of superconducting wire, intentional imperfections in crystalline silicon, or other designs carefully coaxed to behave as quantum systems.

At IonQ, we take a different approach. We use a naturally occurring quantum system: individual atoms.

textSlots.label: TECHNOLOGY / section1 / col3 / col3t
textSlots.defaultValue:
These atoms are the heart of our quantum processing units. We trap them in 3D space, and then use lasers to do everything from initial preparation to final readout.

It requires counterintuitive physics, precision optical and mechanical engineering, and fine-grained firmware control over a variety of components, but the superior results speak for themselves.

textSlots.label: TECHNOLOGY / section2 / panel / pBody1
textSlots.defaultValue: The most important part of any quantum computer are its quantum bits, or qubits. IonQ’s qubits are ionized ytterbium atoms, a silvery rare-earth metal. Each ytterbium atom is perfectly identical to every other ytterbium atom in the universe.

textSlots.label: TECHNOLOGY / section2 / panel / pBody2
textSlots.defaultValue: Moreover, once prepared in a particular stable quantum state, they can remain in that state for very long periods of time — they’re so consistent they’re used in one of the most accurate atomic clocks ever built.

textSlots.label: TECHNOLOGY / section2b / benefitCard1 / d1
textSlots.defaultValue: Reduced error rates mean fewer corrections and more reliable computations.

textSlots.label: TECHNOLOGY / section2b / benefitCard2 / d2
textSlots.defaultValue: Every qubit can interact with every other qubit directly.
